column1: fixtures have wrong warning tags, causing edit issues
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column26:
Originally reported on Google Code with ID 1011
What archive revision are you testing on? (See the revision number next to
"An Archive Of Our Own: Extreme Alpha (rev. #)" in the header). 

rev 1832

What steps will reproduce the problem?
1. With a test database, run rake db:seed
2. Log in as testuser
3. Notice that works are tagged with the old warning tags ("Choose Not To
Warn" etc)
4. Edit the first work (with tag "Choose Not To Warn") -- no warning will
be selected.
5. Hit preview without making any changes
6. "Please add required tags" error comes up. 

This is just because the tags.yml/taggings.yml fixtures are outdated and
need to have the tags corrected to match the new warnings tags. 

Workaround: 

after running rake db:seed, before starting up the archive, also run rake
After:after_change_warning_tag_name

column1: Running challenges and subcollections with nested collections
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column26:
Originally reported on Google Code with ID 1018
Running several different kinds of challenges should now be possible: 

1) A one-shot challenge (eg, Canadian shack)
- create a collection with appropriate settings 
- when challenge is over, close collection

2) An occasionally repeated challenge with separate signups for each one
(eg, Yuletide)
- create a single parent collection and mark it closed
- create subcollections for each challenge with appropriate settings; users
sign up for each subcollection

3) A regularly repeated challenge with a single set of signups (eg, flashfic)
- create a single parent collection for which users sign up
- create subcollections for each new challenge; all users in parent
collection should be able to post to the new subcollection


General notes on subcollections:
- When browsing in a top-level collection, all the works in the
subcollections should come up.
- When browsing in a subcollection, only the works in the subcollection
should come up. 
- Subcollections should be listed on the parent collection's home page.
- Parent collection should be listed on the subcollections' home pages.
- Collections should only be nestable one deep -- ie, you should NOT be
able to make a subcollection the parent of another one. 
- You should be able to create a subcollection from the parent collection's
page.

column1: Anonymity and concealment for collections/challenges
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column26:
Originally reported on Google Code with ID 1019
Collections should allow the moderator to conceal and/or anonymize works in
the archive. 

Concealed Stories:
- On the collection's create/edit page, mark a collection unrevealed. 
- Stories in a collection marked unrevealed should show up as "Mystery
Work" everywhere they are listed for everyone except the author(s). 
- Trying to directly view a story in an unrevealed collection should
produce a page saying "this story will be revealed soon". (The user or an
admin should see the full story beneath.)
- On the home page of a user who has one concealed story and a few other
stories, the filters should NOT include the tags from the concealed story.
- On the works page of the hidden collection, the filters SHOULD include
the tags from the concealed stories. 
- When the collection is reset to be revealed, all stories should appear
normally. 

Anonymized Stories:
- On the collection's create/edit page, mark the collection anonymous.
- Stories in the collection should show up as by "Anonymous" everywhere,
both in blurbs and in displaying the full work. 
- When the collection is set to be not anonymous, all authors should appear
normally.

1. Someone else posts a work inspired by one of yours, and you get a 
notification
2. The notification tells you the title of their work, and their name, and 
the title of your work, and has an approve link.

Example:
Your work I am totally not writing this was listed as the inspiration of 
test  by Cesy

[link]Approve relationship and link back to this work from your work[/link]

For some people, this won't be enough information. For a prolific author, 
the title may not be enough to remind them which story of theirs it was, 
so the title should link to the work. Some people may also wish to see the 
new story before approving the link, so the title of the new work should 
link to it.

1) caching has a long expiry

on the home page, so the page renders with no FOUT, but the font will be cached for
use on the archive, under the hood, so to speak. Then we're not losing new users with
a potentially long first load, but we're also giving them the enriched font face. A

L'

The basic idea here is that we add 'roles' as a means to increase
accessibility for things like subscriptions, inbox, skins, probably if we
add drag&drop collecting/bookmarking/subscribing etc.

lim can add this pretty much immediately but it will throw errors from the

using xhtml 1.0 strict which is the most appropriate doctype for our framework.

Never fear, the answer is to keep the roles and the errors and not stress
about them.

01/Mar/24 8:41 AM;64056257314f50881382f3eb;Currently considering how to achieve this. With works, the preview text is saved as a Draft and then retrieved again for the preview page. We could use jQuery to toggle a view of a preview on the work page, or we can store the comment + work id in {{sessionStorage}}. However, {{sessionStorage}} is not supported pre-IE8. This would avoid a comment draft system as it would not be stored when the session is closed.

If there is another thought/method requirement, let me know, as “as we do for works” is unclear. Does this mean adding a similar draft system for comments (not the worst idea, actually, just more labor, maybe a new ticket) or just rendering on a new page? Or something else entirely?
column107: 20/Apr/24 9:39 AM;64056257314f50881382f3eb;[~accountid:557058:443ab871-4096-403e-bd6f-f3534fe417f0] Hi! I’m not sure who else to ping here. I would love to take this one, but I need clarification on the issue. I asked a few questions in the comment below.
column108:
21/Apr/24 3:51 AM;557058:443ab871-4096-403e-bd6f-f3534fe417f0;[~accountid:64056257314f50881382f3eb] Thanks for the ping! As you can see, this is a really old issue, and tbh it hasn’t had any design consideration at all since it was created 15 years ago and probably should’ve been closed for lack of information. 

Given when this was created and the background of the people working on the Archive at the time, I imagine the thinking was that the user-facing side of comment previews would work like on LiveJournal, but I have no idea what the thinking was for the code side of things. I doubt it was JavaScript (we try to avoid JavaScript-based features), and as you noted, {{sessionStorage}} barely existed at the time, so I doubt that was the thinking, either. It probably _was_ meant to be like work drafts, but we’re not super fond of that system, so I don’t know if we’d still want to go with that.

I will ask around and see if we have any more information for you, or if we can work out a design, but I don’t want to get your hopes up -- this isn’t a very high priority feature, so it might not be something we can fit into our schedule in the near future. I will let you know, though!

column1: Gifts not tracking to users/pseuds properly
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column26:
Originally reported on Google Code with ID 1180
Right now, a gift will show up on your gifts page if the recipient matches
one of your pseud names. There are two problems with this:

1) When you fill in the recipient name on the works form, the autocomplete
suggests bylines, which include the username in parentheses if it doesn't
match the pseud name. Thus if you heed the autocomplete, which presumably
you should, your recipient won't show the gift on their gifts page. :(

2) If there is more than one person with the same pseud name in the
archive, and only the pseud name is entered as the recipient, the gift will
show up on all of their gifts pages, which means that people will show
gifts that aren't actually for them. "You have a gift! Oh no, wait, it's
for the OTHER Rachel, down the street." - we don't really want to do that
to people if we can avoid it. It's depressing.

We should do something about this. Possibly associate the gift with an
actual pseud or user object if we can? Can we reuse some of the same code
we use for co-authors?

I think being unable to scroll the boxes with the arrow/page keys is a problem and

My proposed fix is adding key listeners for the arrow/page keys, to enable keyboard
scrolling when the box is not focused. I have already done this for Opera, and I believe
the only possible negative consequence is that keyboard scrolling happens twice as
fast if the listeners are active and the box is focused (manually). So, the listeners
get removed if the user clicks the box.

I'm unsure about which cases to apply this fix in (Chrome on Macs? Safari? Everything?),
and about how to detect them...user agent sniffing makes me feel bad. If we have any
defined best practices (like, how acceptable is UA sniffing?) and/or anyone who's just
fussy about JS generally, I wouldn't mind some direction. Otherwise, I'll just go with
the feelbad fix, since it is pretty low risk/consequence.

column1: Adding a user to a collection form the owner/moderator interface should make the user Invited, not Member
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column26:
Originally reported on Google Code with ID 1209
What archive revision are you testing on?
r2020

What steps will reproduce the problem?
1. Go to the admin interface for a collection that you own or moderate.
2. Add a user.

What is the expected output? What do you see instead?

Expected: user becomes Invited. A notification should be sent to the user,
with the option to accept or reject the invitation.

Instead: user becomes Member and is immediately listed in the collection's
/people listing.
column101:
12/Jun/10 1:41 AM;557058:6b4e64aa-33bb-449b-9acf-d89ee3ebb29f;I see three parts of this change:
1. Change the default role for a new user to Invited from Member.
2. When a user becomes Invited, send them a notification. Email, or some other means?
A user can become invited by being added, or having their role changed to Invited.
3. Don't show people with a role of Invited or None in the /people section.

Also, to go along with this, should we disallow certain role changes?
There are five possible roles a person can have in a collection:
Owner
Moderator
Member
Invited
None

It makes sense to switch between Owner, Moderator, and Member at will, but not to go
"back" from them to Invited. Should the "None" role be the only one that's allowed
to change to Invited?- **Status changed**: `Assigned`

column1: Tags retain synonym relationship even after being unhooked
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column26:
Originally reported on Google Code with ID 1233
r2050

What steps will reproduce the problem?
1. Take a new tag (with at least 1 work) and make it a canonical. (e.g.
make new work with "Circuses")
2. Take an already-existing canonical tag (with works), un-canonicalize it,
and make it a synonym of the new canonical tag.  Check the "works" listing
for either the canonical or the synonym - it should list all works tagged
with either tag. (e.g. take existing canonical "Circus", de-canonicalize
it, and make it a synonym of "Circuses" - the Works page for either will
show works tagged with either.)
3. On the canonical tag's page, unhook the synonym from the canonical, then
make the synonym into a canonical again. (e.g. make 2 separate canonicals -
"Circus" and "Circuses".)
4. Check the "works" page for the former canonical. It will show some works
for both the canonical and the former synonym-canonical, even though the
tags themselves show no relationship. (e.g. "Circus" only brings up works
tagged "Circus"; but "Circuses" brings up works tagged with "Circus" or
with "Circuses")

This bug is tricky to duplicate, as it seems to depend on the order in
which it's done. Unhooking the canonical from the synonym tag's page
doesn't seem to cause problems.  However, if I unhook the synonym from the
canonical, then I get this effect.

It's happening on the archive now - we had a canonical tag "Pre-Slash",
which was then made a synonym of a new tag "Pre-Relationship". However that
proved confusing for some users, so we made Pre-Slash into its own
canonical again. However, the filter for "Pre-Relationship" still brings up
many works only tagged "Pre-Slash":

http://archiveofourown.org/tags/Pre-Relationship/works

even though if you look at the tags themselves, they are not synonyms and
there is no visible relationship between the tags:
http://archiveofourown.org/tags/Pre-Relationship/edit
http://archiveofourown.org/tags/Pre-Slash/edit

09/Jun/10 1:33 AM;557058:33aa6c27-2fd0-479b-b291-1f8e13db0fe4;Okey dokey.

We have a bigger problem on our hands:

We currently want to validate as XHTML 1.0 Strict, which does not support modularisation
as it is defined by XHTML 1.1. The best way to support ARIA and embed attributes would
be to put them on our html declaration, but this _will not_ validate under any circumstances
as xmlns has a fixed definition in XHTML 1.0 Strict. Alternatively, we can raise a
broader code issue, and move to XHTML 1.1, and then write our own DTD.- **Labels added**: ADTAttentionRequired

column108:
25/Jul/10 11:57 PM;557058:33aa6c27-2fd0-479b-b291-1f8e13db0fe4;More info for AD&T!

We currently serve our XHTML 1.0 as text/html, which limits our ability to use any
of the supported XML functions because the browsers on the other end believe text/html
== HTML 4.0. We do this to have maximum compatibility with IE, which is XML-incompetent.
See http://www.colincochrane.com/post/2007/11/10/Internet-Explorer-7-Did-Not-Kill-XHTML.aspx
and the Wikipedia article on IE 8. Note no support for XHTML as application/xml, which
is what XHTML 1.1 demands.

So, what does this mean for ARIA support & validation? It means we can't validate as
we stand, even though our ARIA roles are working, but we also can't move up, because
moving to XHTML 1.1. would break our pages in IE.

I'll leave this issue open because the situation may change in the future.

-- on the work itself it should say "Part of a series (hidden)"
-- the other works in the series if any should link "over" the story
-- the author can see the series when they edit the work

- If a series is empty because all its works are hidden, the series WILL still appear on the user's home page (so it can be edited)

When you implement this behavior please uncomment the deferred tests in collection_anonymity.feature!

column1: Remove a co-author from a chapter
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column26:
Currently, if you want to remove yourself as a chapter co-creator, you have to go to the work's Manage Chapters page, where you will find a "Remove Me As Author" button on any chapters you co-created. 

That's both hard to find and confusingly-named, so we want to change it to "Remove Me As Chapter Co-Creator" _and_ put a "Remove Me As Chapter Co-Creator" option on the Edit page for any chapters you co-created.

When you click the "Remove Me As Chapter Co-Creator" link, the confirmation pop-up should say, "Are you sure you want to remove yourself as a co-creator of this chapter?"

When you choose "OK" in the pop-up, you should get a blue flash message that says, "You have been removed as a creator from the chapter."

The chapter byline should also update.

----
 

Old information retained for record keeping:

{quote}Originally reported on Google Code with ID 1262
You should be able to post a new chapter that is just by you (i.e. remove 
the co-author) when there is a co-author for earlier chapters in the work. 
You should also be able to edit a chapter and remove another co-author 
from a chapter.

(You shouldn't be able to do this for the whole work, just for individual 
chapters in it.){quote}

22/Aug/16 6:45 PM;557058:443ab871-4096-403e-bd6f-f3534fe417f0;We don't want to let you remove other people as co-authors -- you can't do that with works, either. But you can currently remove yourself as a chapter co-author by going to the work's Edit page at http://test.ao3.org/works/###/edit and following Manage Chapters to http://test.ao3.org/works/###/chapters/manage. Right now, there's a "Remove Me As Author" link for every chapter, regardless of whether you're a co-author on that chapter, but clicking it on one you're not co-author of won't do any damage.

For the pull request, I've changed the text to the clearer and less-text-centric (although lord knows Chapter is pretty text-y) "Remove Me As Chapter Co-Creator" and added the link to the top of individual chapters' Edit pages as well. On both the Manage Chapters and Edit Chapter pages, the button should only appear if you are actually a co-creator of that chapter.

I've also changed the confirmation message to just ask if you're sure -- it used to say you would no longer be able to edit the chapter, but that is a lie. 23/Apr/12 7:12 PM;557058:c714f0f0-b42d-45c7-be2f-d002135599e4;Okay, so the problem here is that there's a validation in the filter count model which
should prevent more than one filter count from being created for a given tag. However,
as was the case with user logins, it's not actually preventing duplicates from being
created 100% of the time, and when that happens, both objects are invalid, which causes
problems down the line. The solution is to actually turn the index on filter_id into
a unique index so that the database will act as the bouncer here, since it does a much
better job of it than the application does.

Note: it is EXTREMELY IMPORTANT to make sure we clean out the duplicates before we
run the migration that changes the index, otherwise the migration will fail in the
middle of the deploy, which we don't want.

There's probably no way for testers to test this once it's done - we can just verify
that the fandoms page still works and that nothing blew up.- **Labels removed**: NeedsTests

column1: No way to edit info or tags on an External Work bookmark
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column26:
Originally reported on Google Code with ID 1273
r2101

What steps will reproduce the problem?
1. Make a new external bookmark
2. Enter author, summary, tags, etc. & "create" bookmark
3. When you edit the bookmark, you can edit  "Your Tags" and "Your Notes"
but cannot edit the other fields of the External Work.

The only way to change this info is to make a new bookmark. The information
originally entered also auto-fills whenever anyone else enters that
address.  Even if you delete the original bookmark, the original External
Works information will come up when the web address is entered as a New
Bookmark.  So if, say, the author's name or the work's title is mispelled,
there is no way to correct it without making a new bookmark, and anyone who
enters that same address in the future will get the original mispelled
info, not the corrected data.

Additionally, if you make a typo in one of the External Work tags, there is
no way to correct the tag, and it will remain in the system even after you
delete the bookmark; it will not be raked.

Users need some way to edit External Works data.

relationships between two canonical tags of the same category. Details:

1) A tag inherits its meta-tags' meta-tags. (The database keeps track of
which are direct and which are inherited, but that's not displayed yet.)

with it.

sub-tags. When the relationship is removed, the filters should also be
removed from the works.

**********************


It should now be possible to:

- Make a collection (or a subcollection) into a Gift Exchange in the
collection settings

- Create signup settings for the Gift Exchange including instructions,
specific tags, limits on number of tags of various kinds, and required
descriptions or urls.

-- The collection is unmoderated
-- The collection is moderated and the user is a member

see a "Join" link instead. Once they have been made a member by the
moderator, they should then see the Sign Up link.) 

- In the signup form, users should see:
-- if the moderator put in specific tags for a given type of tag,
checkboxes for those tags
-- text input fields for other types of tags that the moderator allowed
-- a textarea for optional tags if the moderator allowed that (not if the
moderator didn't)
-- a text input field/textarea for url/description if the moderator allowed
that (not if the moderator didn't) 

- When signing up, users should get error messages if they:
-- use non-canonical tags
-- use the wrong number of tags 

- If a user has signed up, they should then see "edit/cancel signup" links
in the collection and be able to edit the signup without having to re-enter
everything from scratch.

- If a user goes to the new signup url after signing up the first time,
they should be redirected to their existing signup.

- The owners/maintainers of the collection should be able to see a list of
all the signed-up users.

16/Oct/12 12:17 AM;557058:563cc0f0-cad4-465b-b3f4-47e1e66c2d4a;While creators usually feel very protective of the feedback they get (and being able
to move them when fixing posting errors would be convenient), the comments technically
don't belong to them. Attaching them to a different chapter without the comment creator's
consent has abuse implications that we might have to address before going ahead with
this design.

My suggestion, should the creator wish to conserve comments (Y/N), would be to attach
them to the currently *last* chapter (standard procedure when a comment is posted to
the "whole" work, i.e. in full view), or the chapter directly after the deleted one.
The latter option would vaguely preserve the comments' place in the commenting timeline,
while the former would probably be easier to implement and less confusing. In both
cases, they'd get permanently moved to the appropriate place with a "$user commented
on a deleted chapter" heading. - **Status changed**: `PendingReview`

24/Aug/12 2:57 PM;557058:c714f0f0-b42d-45c7-be2f-d002135599e4;Just wanted to clarify: are Tag1 and Tag2 synonyms in this scenario? New!search lets

column1: Hide/show warnings produces malformed html in various blurbs
column11: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
column26:
Originally reported on Google Code with ID 1372
What archive revision are you testing on?
r2312

What steps will reproduce the problem?
1. Post a work with at least two archive warnings and at least two freeform
(additional) tags.
2. Log in as a different user (because authors can't hide warnings or tags
on own works) and select preferences to hide warnings and freeform tags by
default.
3. Browse any page that shows works warnings (/works, /bookmarks etc.)
4. Click to reveal warnings.

What is the expected output? What do you see instead?

In IE8, if there are at least two hidden tags, the warnings don't expand at
all.

In other browsers they open, but the resulting html is still malformed -
the span used for hiding doesn't nest properly with open and close list items.

This is actually back end, because the code is malformed. It's just that
some browsers cope better with it than others.

that we're running the parser on imported html, which is not the same as text entered

column99:
22/Mar/10 7:25 AM;557058:1804058f-89f5-4734-8604-8bb294f3deef;Actually, this *is* a parser problem (well, currently): 

One, we don't know what kind of source was imported. If plain text was imported then
we would need to put in paragraph breaks also. If we are importing stories out of a
database (ie, importing an archive from db) then that db might (like we currently do)
store works exactly as entered without user-entered paragraph breaks, in which case
ditto. 

Two, the parser currently works only on output, not input. At that point we can't
really tell whether a work has been imported or not, and in any case, we still want
the parser's sanitizing functions. 

IIRC, the previous parser manually stripped doubled-up/empty paragraphs/breaks, which
is probably the best temporary solution until we move to parse-once-on-input.

06/Apr/10 5:21 PM;557058:1804058f-89f5-4734-8604-8bb294f3deef;"I set it to match on 1 request and 1 fandom, expecting that it would only match
on both, but I got assignments where it only matched on request not fandom"

To clarify: a request is a bundle of tags. An individual request won't match unless
the criteria for matching tags is met. The multiple requests matching is intended for
a case like Yuletide where people put in four very separate requests. 

In the example you are showing, the requester doesn't *have* any fandoms. The code
considers everyone a match in that case, which IMO is the right choice because it
allows for a challenge where eg, someone putting in Jack Harkness as their character
request with no fandom would match someone who offered Dr. Who as fandom and Jack
Harkness as character. If as a challenge mod you really wanted to require people to
match only on fandom, you'd need to require them to at least one fandom in their
signups. So this is wont-fix. 

"I've mentioned this elsewhere (issue 1537), but the generator should try to match
everyone up with a recipient when there is an odd number of participants, instead of
leaving one person out."

This is wont-fix also: code to ensure an ideal/complete match would be truly
prohibitively slow for all but the tiniest of challenges. (It would require code that
in the worst-case would end up calculating every set of assignments among all
potential matches, because that is the only way to be sure there isn't a complete
match out there you haven't found.) 

So instead, matching works on a best-approximation process that can then be
hand-tweaked very easily as much as the maintainer wants. Generally it matches all
but a small handful of people even for huge challenges. 

"Also we should not get circular matching (A to B, B to A) unless
this is the best way to match everyone up."

Can you pop in a new issue for avoiding circular matching? I can put something in to
try and avoid that where possible, but I think it should be lower priority.

to A. I had one set where all participants were matched circularly thus,
with one person not assigned because they were the odd one out.

part of the point of participating in a group gift challenge is to exchange
gifts with different people.

We want the archive to remain a noncommercial space. 
TO
We want the Archive to remain a non-commercial space.

TO
We welcome feedback from Archive user at Content Policy. The link to

http://transformativeworks.org/contact/content%20policy

Nonobjectionable fanworks are not removed from the site when a user is

TO
Non-objectionable fanworks are not removed from the site when a user is
suspended. Suspended users who wish to delete or orphan their fanworks may

tags. As a site user, you will see user tags in several different
situations. These are the current plans: (1) You'll be able to search tags
generally, so you'll be able to find fanworks that anyone, whether creator
or user, has labelled "wingfic." (2) When you're browsing and looking at
story summaries, you'll see tags from the author as well as tags from other
users to whose tags you've chosen to subscribe. (3) When you're looking at
a given user's bookmark for a particular fanwork, you'll be able to see
that user's tags.
TO
Please place items (1), (2), and (3) in an ordered list.

As with all other content, creators' decisions are presumed reasonable, and
using "not rated"/"choose not to warn" will always be sufficient.
TO
As with all other content, creators' decisions are presumed reasonable, and
using "not rated" or "chose not to use Archive warnings" will always be
sufficient.

See our Open Doors FAQ. 
TO
Refer to our Open Doors FAQ.

18/Jan/11 4:27 PM;557058:56c6aaf0-abec-4140-88a3-59aa2f24c990;Ahah! This happens (at least sometimes?) when a synonym tag is moved from one canonical
to another (i.e. when a tag's "Synonym of" field is changed) - the works filter relationship
is not switching over.

Example: take tag "AU - 1940s" - http://testarchive.transformativeworks.org/tags/AU%20-%201940s
 a synonym of "Alternate Universe - 1940s" appearing in this filter:
http://testarchive.transformativeworks.org/tags/Alternate%20Universe%20-%201940s/works

Edit http://testarchive.transformativeworks.org/tags/AU%20-%201940s/edit to Synonym
of "Alternate Universe - 1920s" and then click "Works".

3 works show up in the http://testarchive.transformativeworks.org/tags/AU%20-%201920s/works
filter, but the work tagged with "AU - 1940s" does not appear. However it no longer
appears in http://testarchive.transformativeworks.org/tags/Alternate%20Universe%20-%201940s/works
either. The synonym tag looks correct, but any works tagged with it will not appear
in any filters.

The same thing happens when you try to make a new canonical off a synonym tag already
tied to a canonical - e.g. if on http://testarchive.transformativeworks.org/tags/AU%20-%201940s/edit
you enter "AU 1940s Test Tag" in the "Synonym of" field, the system will create a canonical
"AU 1940s Test Tag", but its filter will bring up 0 works, despite the synonym having
one work attached.

To make the filters work properly, the synonym relationship must be removed entirely
(synonym field cleared), the tag saved, then the canonical synonym added and the tag
saved again; then the tagged work shows properly in the canonical's filter. 

The work filters should automatically change when the tag's synned canonical is changed.- **Labels added**: Roadmap-TagWrangling, Access-TagWrangler

column108:
16/Jul/11 2:47 PM;557058:327d6059-0150-4fe5-8791-0d5e6025a597;This is a very complex problem, not so much because of what causes the issue but because
the issue permeates so many levels.

E.g. here are two related bugs I've found:
- Deleting tags on work will not (always) properly delete filters on work
- Adding tags that are meta tags to tags that already exist on the work will not be
properly set to be direct filters (they are still set to be inherited)

The main issue here is that properly removing a tag and all metatags without removing
those metatags that are still needed cannot be done the way it's implemented now. At
the moment we loop over the metatags and check if some of their subtags are still in
the filters list. However that will of course be the case if those subtags also happen
to be metatags of the original tag that should be removed. And we can't just ignore
all metatags of the original tag to remove because there might still be remaining tags
on the work that also have those metatags.

The rather simple solution is to get an up-to-date list of all meta tags from the current
list of tags minus the one to be removed. Then all filters/meta tags not in that list
can safely be removed.

What archive revision are you testing on? (See the revision number next to

If appropriate, enter the URL of a page where the problem can be seen:
http://archiveofourown.org/admin/settings (You can only actually see the
problem in action if you are an admin on Beta Archive, but you don't need
those powers to make the fix.)

1. Look at where it says '30 people are scheduled to be sent invitations on
$DATE'.
2. Feel perplexed, because $DATE is some time in the past, but the
invitations queue is running happily. 

$DATE is calculated from the last time the invitations queue sent out
invitations, but if the job is interrupted and then resumed, this throws
the date out. The date should be calcuated from time.now + frequency, not
the old time + frequency. 

The fix needs to be applied in the rake task for invitations, on the line:

new_date = AdminSetting.invite_from_queue_at +
(AdminSetting.invite_from_queue_frequency).days


Please also add some logging so that when the job issues invitations, it
records having done so.

in its publication date being set to its creation date.

I went with created_at over Date.today because using the latter would mean that every
time a work is un-backdated (say you edit it multiple times and toggle the option repeatedly),
its publication date changes to today, no matter how old the work is or when it was

column26:

2. Make one of your other pseuds default.
3. Try to make that other pseud non-default again.

What is the expected output? What do you see instead?

I would expect the other pseud to become default again.

Instead an error occurs.

This is because when a user remains without any default pseud, the code tries to make
default the pseud that has the same name as the username, which fails when the user
has changed their username.

15/Dec/10 1:17 PM;557058:be6d5da9-c318-4a37-90a3-f06f5f84c0eb;the underlying error is that when you change your username you don't get a new pseud
to match. 

because of Issue 1817, about half our users don't have default pseuds. for those users,
if they change their username and then delete the old pseud (which they can now do
as it is neither default nor matches their username) they will end up with no pseuds

30/Aug/11 3:42 PM;557058:733fae5a-a08d-4a3b-91e0-914bfc0ce3a2;https://otw.16bugs.com/projects/4911/bugs/197966

I’ve established that a couple of major ebook readers can’t parse epubs with internal
files bigger than 300kb. (This is a known issue of those ebook readers.) (Sonys and
Jinke-derivatives; haven’t had the chance to try a Nook.)

(To understand what I’m talking about, grab any chaptered fic, download as epub, change
the .epub extension to .zip, and unzip. Inside the OEBPS folder will be several HTML
files. If those are bigger than 300kb, the ebook won’t work on some ebook readers.)

This is roughly 45,000 words. While ebook readers can handle (pretty much) any size
of file, if any one chapter is bigger than ~45k words, it’ll freeze up or have other
problems. (IIRC, a Sony won’t open the file; my PEZ opens & reads until it hits the
300kb mark and then stops mid-word.)

The epub export function automatically splits chapters into separate sections. Single-chaptered
works don’t get split. I’m not sure there’s an easy solution to this (Calibre splits
into separate HTML files that have no connection to chapter breaks, which is annoying),
but it’s worth knowing what causes the “my ebook reader can’t read those files” problem.

If it matters, the work I discovered/tested this on is archiveofourown.org/works/156093

.mobi files don’t have this problem, because the way .mobi is read by the software
is different.

25/Sep/11 11:05 AM;557058:f9f1d36a-b0f4-4a02-baf1-e70adc58ae89;Reproduced on a Sony PRS-350 with this work: archiveofourown.org/works/205389

I'm going to investigate this. Splitting chapters into several html files when they
grow too big doesn't seem too annoying. (On my Sony, all I notice is page breaks, and
one seemingly random page break per 45.000 words isn't a bad tradeoff, provided one
can do it without messing up the html too much.) Oh, and I want to add that it's not
a problem with the overall size of the work, just with the chapter size.

column99:
08/Nov/10 10:34 AM;557058:be6d5da9-c318-4a37-90a3-f06f5f84c0eb;I've taken care of the first one. epub files (and mobi's)  have separate pages for summary
and meta only when they are chaptered. For single chaptered works, this looks much
better, but it still allows you to have a table of contents on multi-chaptered works.

As for making it look pretty, a front-end coder can take this issue now! :)

Some constraints:

no per-person customizing (no "if current_user" logic). If someone wants a personalized
skin, they can download the html and fix it up themselves before converting it.

the styles are in the file /app/views/layouts/barebones.html.erb. All styles must be
in the header element, you can't link to stylesheets.

remember, some readers will ignore styles altogether, and typically the font and text
size will be overridden on the device as well.

the views are in /app/views/works/

download.html.erb is for any html and pdf download, and for single chaptered mobi and
epub downloads. In these cases, the same rendered html is created, and then the non-html
formats are converted. This means if someone else comes back later and wants a different
format for the same work, much of the work has already been done.

download.html.erb calls the following partials, which are also used directly in the
mobi and epub formats for chaptered works.
 
_download_preface.html.erb
_download_chapter.html.erb  (once per chapter)
_download_afterword.html.erb

for chaptered works only, you can customize the formatting for mobi files with the
@mobi instance variable (I found putting chapter titles in mobi chapters caused duplication.)

column26:
Originally reported on Google Code with ID 1951
As of revision 3249:

Gift exchanges now offer the following new options to moderators setting them up:

- Allow users to offer/request an "Any" option which will match anything on the other
side. Help file added to explain this option to users.

- Require unique values across requests/offers (ie "all fandoms must be unique").

- Initialize fandom, character, relationship, and freeform tag lists to those which
are either above/below the average in popularity. This process runs in the background
and can be slow; if it doesn't immediately produce results, wait ~10 minutes and refresh
the challenge settings page. A help file has been added to explain the process. 

- Restrict character/relationship tags to those wrangled to the selected fandom. If
this option is enabled, then in the signup form, if a fandom is selected in a request/offer,
the autocomplete will try to only show characters in that fandom; there is also validation
on prompts to ensure that no characters outside the fandom can be submitted even if
the autocomplete happens to deliver them. 


The matching and assignments pages have also been updated: 

- Control links/buttons have been renamed hopefully to be more clear. (Save Assignment
Changes, Show Assigned Pinch Hits, etc)

- If matching fails and is canceled, refreshing the page should now allow a moderator
to get back to the "Generate Matches" option instead of being locked out. 

- In the defaulted assignments list, users should now be listed with a notation if
they were a pinch recipient or a pinch hitter (so ie, if a recipient appears twice,
it will be clear why).

Fixed in revision 3299 and revision 3303

- "Any Character", "Any Freeform" etc should now appear at same font size as the tags
in the signups listing.

- Signups are now paginated 20 to a page, and in alphabetical order by pseud.

- By default, URLs and descriptions are now hidden and can be shown using the "Show
[X]" button at the top of each page.
